# PgReturnedRowsUsedAsAffectedRows

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Identify pg_num_rows on unchanged successful pg_query result whose constant SQL is INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE without RETURNING. Parse literals/comments rather than substring matching.

## Detection

- D1. Report pg_num_rows on unchanged successful pg_query result whose constant SQL is INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE without RETURNING. Parse literals/comments rather than substring matching.
- D2. Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods, including imports and supported named arguments. Follow only bounded local facts within one lexical scope. Receiver and argument provenance must establish the specific API contract; variable names and comments never prove intent.
- D3. Report one finding per violating operation. A reachable path, unchanged value identity and applicable API behavior are required. Intervening mutation, unknown calls involving tracked values, escaped aliases or exhausted analysis budgets invalidate proof.

## Exceptions (no report)

- E1. Exclude unresolved required symbols, user-defined lookalikes, incomplete syntax, unknown required values and unsupported versions. Cases outside D1 receive no finding.
- E2. Both `@custos-ignore PgReturnedRowsUsedAsAffectedRows` and `@noinspection PgReturnedRowsUsedAsAffectedRows` suppress this native rule.
- E3. A value the shared flow analysis proves is not the failure value at the use is never reported, whatever form the proof takes: a test in an enclosing branch, loop condition or short-circuit operand, an early exit, a statement that leaves on the failing outcome (`$v !== false or exit;`, `$v or throw …;`, `$v ?: throw …;`), a failing branch that ends in a call that never returns (a callee declared `never`, or a function or a final or private method every path of which throws or exits), a test stored in a boolean and tested later while neither the boolean nor the tested variable has been written, and, on PHP 8.0 and later outside any `try` with a `catch`, a builtin call that returned after receiving the value for a parameter that only accepts arrays, objects or callables: such a call throws a `TypeError` for `false`. A `switch (true)` case is read like the condition of an `if`/`elseif` chain; in a `switch` on the variable itself with constant labels, the cases after a `false` or `null` label and the `default` hold a value that is neither, as does a `true` case. Positions PHP may skip prove nothing: the right side of `??=`, the arguments of a null-safe call and anything chained after `?->`. A null-safe call to a never-returning method does not end the path, and `f(...)` creates a closure without calling `f`.

## Fix

None. A repair requires a semantic decision or application error-handling policy.

## PHP versions

Available in PHP 5.3–8.5 where the referenced API exists. Do not apply extension contracts when the resolved API is unavailable. Gate syntax and version-specific behavior to the configured target.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "PgReturnedRowsUsedAsAffectedRows": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore PgReturnedRowsUsedAsAffectedRows
```
